question: In a small FMU counterfactual placement set, does a prospective coolant+primary-flow peak predictor choose a different rack from state-blind round-robin, and what are the measured outcomes when it does?
scope: FMU thermal placement relevance only; no RAPS scheduler, Task 1.6, acceptance change, or RL

training_data.method: ridge alpha 1.0, predictor standardization on training set, unpenalized intercept; freeze coefficients and training hashes before any new scenario FMU run
training_data.internal_check: leave-one-state-out errors on the 13 available states; descriptive only because training states are correlated

scenario_preconditioning.other_rack_context_scope: all racks except candidate racks 1 and 44

counterfactual_branches.offered_load: step exactly one chosen candidate rack from 10.86 to 40.0 kW; all other racks remain 10.86 kW
counterfactual_branches.effect_definition: candidate placement branch minus same-state no-step control

decision_rules.blind: the listed round-robin rack choice for each ordered scenario, without reading FMU observations
decision_rules.aware: use the frozen coolant+flow model to predict absolute peak coolant for each candidate rack; choose lower predicted peak; on equality within 1e-9 C choose lower predicted final; on another tie choose lower rack ID
decision_rules.model_limit: The primary-flow feature is identical for both candidates within one scenario. In an additive model it cancels from their ranking; this design tests coolant-informed ranking against round-robin, not the incremental decision value of primary flow.

primary_metrics: number of scenarios where blind and aware rules choose different racks
for every scenario and especially disagreements: aware minus blind actual absolute peak coolant of the placed rack over 0-3600 s
aware minus blind actual maximum coolant across all 44 racks over 0-3600 s
secondary_metrics: placed-rack absolute final coolant and paired peak/final incremental response
predicted scores and ranking margins for both candidate racks
oracle best-of-two peak outcome as an analysis reference, not a third policy
complete power, FMU heat-input, rack coolant, CDU primary supply/return, and primary-flow trajectories
two fresh-process repeats and source/data hashes
interpretation: No pass/fail threshold selected from outcomes. If choices do not differ or actual peak differences are negligible, report a negative relevance result. A difference in this FMU counterfactual is not yet a RAPS closed-loop scheduler benefit. No causal flow claim or RL claim.
stop_gate: Stop after this experiment for research review; no Task 1.5 revision, Task 1.6, history experiment, scheduler implementation, or RL.
